disease_details.evidence_quote: AN is characterized by distorted body image, reduced food intake, loss of body weight. classified into restricting (AN-RS) type and binge-eating or purging (AN-BP) type
disease_details.notes: Two major AN subtypes are present in the cohort; healthy controls represent baseline

disease_response_orr.notes: This field applies to treatment response in cancer trials; AN is not a cancer condition and no ORR metric is reported

disease_response_pfs.notes: PFS is a cancer-specific endpoint; not applicable to AN study

disease_response_pfs_month.notes: Not applicable; AN is not a malignancy

disease_response_recist.notes: RECIST criteria apply to solid tumors; not relevant to AN study

feces_phenotype.evidence_quote: Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics performed on faecal and serum samples from 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females
feces_phenotype.notes: Multiple faecal phenotypes measured including bacterial taxa, virome, functional modules, and structural variants

fmt_id.evidence_quote: Faecal samples from three patients with AN (females aged 20, 22 and 20 yr with BMI 10.3, 11.5 and 11.7 kg/m²) and three HC (females aged 20, 22 and 21 yr with BMI 22.6, 21.1 and 21.2 kg/m²)
fmt_id.notes: IDs assigned for donor identification; exact identifiers not explicitly given in paper

fmt_role.evidence_quote: Faecal microbiota from AN cases and HC to germ-free mice. 250 mg faecal samples suspended and transferred to mice recipients
fmt_role.notes: Human donors provided faecal material for FMT; germ-free mice were recipients

hla.notes: HLA typing not performed or reported in this study

neonatal_birth_weight.notes: Study enrolled adults and adolescents diagnosed with AN; neonatal measures not collected

neonatal_delivery_procedure.notes: Not applicable; study focuses on adult/adolescent AN patients, not neonatal cohorts

neonatal_feeding_method.notes: Early infant feeding history not reported in this AN population study

neonatal_gestational_age.notes: Not applicable; subjects were adolescent/adult women with AN diagnosis

neonatal_preterm_birth.notes: Birth history not collected in this cross-sectional adult/adolescent study

obgyn_birth_control.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria for healthy controls: regular medication apart from birth control pills
obgyn_birth_control.notes: Birth control pills were specifically allowed in healthy controls; AN patients' birth control status not explicitly stated

obgyn_menopause.notes: Menopausal status not explicitly reported; cohort includes women with EDI-3 validated for ages 13-53

obgyn_pregnancy.notes: Current pregnancy status not reported in study

smoker.evidence_quote: Covariates including age, BMI, smoking and multiple drug intake were deconfounded
smoker.notes: Smoking status was collected as a covariate but detailed prevalence by group not reported

treatment.evidence_quote: Care by multidisciplinary team with customized meals, cognitive behavioural therapy. Medications: selective serotonin re-uptake inhibitors, antipsychotics, benzodiazepines
treatment.section: Methods — Study participants (In-patients and Out-patients sections)
treatment.notes: AN patients received medications and psychotherapy; medication effects deconfounded in analyses

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: Not applicable; AN is a psychiatric eating disorder, not a malignancy

tumor_staging_tnm.notes: TNM staging does not apply to eating disorders

value: HOMA-IR (Homeostatic Model Assessment for Insulin Resistance)
biomarker_name.evidence_quote: Serum glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR, C-reactive protein measured. Metabolomics revealed indole-3-propionic acid, bile acids. Metagenomics profiled bacterial taxa, viral species, functional modules, structural variants
biomarker_name.notes: Extensive multi-omics biomarkers measured including serum metabolites, bacterial abundance, viral composition, and genetic variants

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: Serum biochemical analyses, metabolomics profiling, relative abundance measured from metagenomics. Beta-diversity calculated as Canberra distance
biomarker_unit.section: Methods — Biochemical analyses, Metabolomics, Statistical analysis
biomarker_unit.notes: Specific units inferred from measurement types; not all explicitly stated for each biomarker

value: Higher insulin sensitivity (lower HOMA-IR) in AN
Higher bile acid concentrations in AN
Clostridium positively correlated with eating disorder scores
Lower predicted growth rates in 6 bacterial species in AN
85 overlapping ASVs transferred from human to mouse
53 Lactococcus phage species enriched in AN

AN (Anorexia Nervosa): Reduced weight gain in FMT mice on energy-restricted diet
HC (Healthy Controls): More abundant Roseburia and butyrate producers

biomarker_value.evidence_quote: Women with AN were leaner, had lower glucose, lower insulin, higher insulin sensitivity, lower C-reactive protein. Multiple bacterial taxa altered in AN. Serum indole-3-propionic acid increased in AN. GF mice with AN FMT showed larger initial weight decrease, slower weight gain
biomarker_value.section: Results — Phenotypes, Gut microbiota composition, Serum metabolites, FMT experiments
biomarker_value.notes: Values derived from comparative statistical analyses between AN and HC groups

disease_response_os.notes: This is a cross-sectional mechanistic study; long-term survival outcomes not tracked

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status primarily used in cancer trials; not reported for AN cohort

value: Lower Roseburia intestinalis and Roseburia inulinivorans
Higher β-diversity at genus and species level
Higher R-enterotype (Ruminococcaceae-enterotype) prevalence in AN vs HC
Higher β-diversity in AN-BP compared to AN-RS
219 viral-bacterial interactions in HC vs 84 in AN
25 of 30 increased viral species in AN are Lactococcus phages
Higher Chao1 richness and Shannon diversity in AN virome
Reduced PTR (growth rate) in 6 bacterial species in AN
5,056 deletion SVs and 2,423 variable SVs identified across 56 species
Significant beta-diversity difference in SV composition between AN and HC

AN (Anorexia Nervosa): Reduced Bacteroidota and Actinobacteriota at phylum level

feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: AN microbiota characterized by reduction in Bacteroidota, enriched Christensenellaceae, higher Lactobacillus. HC microbiota enriched in Roseburia, Faecalibacterium. AN had 219 HC vs 84 AN viral-bacterial interactions. 85 overlapping ASVs transferred human to mouse
feces_phenotype_value.section: Results — Gut microbiota composition, Viral microbiota, Bacterial growth rates, Structural variants, FMT experiments
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Comprehensive microbiota phenotypes quantified by shotgun metagenomics and 16S amplicon sequencing

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; AN is not a malignancy

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; study focuses on gut microbiota in anorexia nervosa, not tumor measurements.

value: Study included 77 female AN cases and 70 age-matched healthy female controls
Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics performed on faecal and serum samples
Faecal microbiota transplantation from AN cases to germ-free mice under energy-restricted feeding
Danish cohort; only Caucasian women included
Recruited from three specialized eating disorder centres in Denmark from 1 September 2014 to 31 July 2016
All AN patients met DSM-5 criteria for restricting or binge/purging subtypes
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females; shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics were performed on faecal and serum samples, respectively

study_name.notes: Study identifier name not explicitly stated; study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02217384).

curator.notes: No curator information provided in the paper.

target_condition.evidence_quote: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is an eating disorder with a high mortality.

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: Microbial DNAs were isolated and purified from stool samples using NucleoSpin soil mini kit
dna_extraction_kit.section: Methods — DNA extraction, 16S rRNA sequencing and data analyses in mice experiments
dna_extraction_kit.notes: For human faecal samples: DNA extraction followed IHMS SOP P7 V2. For mouse samples: NucleoSpin soil mini kit (MACHEREY‑NAGEL) was used.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: Purified and amplified DNA fragment libraries were sequenced using the Ion Proton Sequencer
sequencing_platform.notes: Ion Proton Sequencer used for shotgun metagenomics of human faecal samples. Separately, 16S rRNA sequencing of mouse samples was performed on Illumina MiSeq.

host_species.evidence_quote: shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics were performed on faecal and serum samples from a cohort of 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females
host_species.notes: Primary cohort is human; study also includes mouse experiments (faecal microbiota transplantation to germ-free mice), but the main study population is human.

extraction_warnings: No individual subject_id or sample_id values provided in paper; data reported only as aggregate group statistics (n=77 AN, n=70 HC). Sample-level granularity reflects the categorical grouping structure, not per-individual data.

Age reported only as 'age-matched' in Methods; no specific age values, mean, or range given. Age_group inferred as 'Adult' based on context (EDI-3 designed for ages 13–53, clinical treatment setting suggests primarily older adolescents/adults).

BMI values not provided in supplementary table; only reported that AN cases 'were much leaner' with lower fasting glucose/insulin. Control BMI range specified as 18.5–25 kg/m² (inclusion criterion) but not as measured values.
Exact country 'Denmark' confirmed in Methods; specific cities (Odense, Aarhus, Aalborg) mentioned as recruitment sites for AN cases but not for controls.

Antibiotic exclusion criterion applied: 'antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months' excluded for AN cases; 'antibiotics within the last 3 months' excluded for controls. Coded as antibiotics_current_use='No' to reflect this.
Disease assignment: AN cases classified as 'Case' with disease list ['Anorexia Nervosa']; controls classified as 'Study Control' with disease list ['Healthy'].
Ancestry 'Danish Caucasian' explicitly stated in inclusion criteria; mapped to European ancestry with detailed specification.
FMT mouse experiments (Extended Data Fig. 9) not included in sample extraction as they involve germ-free animal recipients, not human participants matching the schema.
Batch 1 returned granularity='subgroup_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

Batch 1 subgroups ['AN (Anorexia Nervosa)', 'HC (Healthy Controls)', 'AN-RS (Restricting Subtype)', 'AN-BP (Binge-Eating/Purging Subtype)', 'AN-T (AN-Transplanted Mice)', 'HC-T (HC-Transplanted Mice)'] differ from batch 0 []; kept batch 0.
Paper is a human and mouse mechanistic study of AN pathogenesis; many oncology-specific fields (ORR, PFS, RECIST, TNM, tumor size, ECOG) are not applicable.
FMT study had only 3 donors per group and 10 recipients per group; mouse study is small and mechanistic rather than clinical trial.
Neonatal and obstetric fields not applicable; cohort consists of adolescent and adult women with diagnosed AN.
Specific numerical biomarker values reported as group comparisons (AN vs HC) rather than individual sample values; granularity is study_level within each group.
Birth control use confirmed allowed in HC exclusion criteria but AN patients' contraceptive use not explicitly stated.
No HLA typing or tumor staging performed; these fields are domain-specific to immunology and oncology respectively.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
The study is not a tumor/cancer study; tumor_size_residual_measurement field is not applicable but was required to evaluate.
Study name is not explicitly provided; ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT02217384 is available.
Two host species are represented (human primary cohort and mouse FMT experiments); extracted 'Human' for the main study population.
